newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Rival queries Indonesia party claim on seat numbers.
newsitem.headline: Rival queries Indonesia party claim on seat numbers.

text.p: A claim by an Indonesian minority party that it had receive enough votes to reach the minimum number of seats required in the parliament has been questioned by a rival party, the Kompas newspaper reported on Sunday.

The government faction of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) said on Saturday it had obtained additional votes in North Sumatra province and could now reach the minimum level of 11 legislators according to parliamentary rules.
The future of the PDI has been in question since its vote was decimated at the May 29 national election after a fracture in the party last year.

Its poor showing in the violence-tainted election campaign and the collapse of its vote in the poll amid claims of irregularities saw the number of PDI legislators in the national parliament fall from 56 to an estimated 10 members.
But the rival Moslem-orientated United Development Party (PPP) said its figures showed the PDI had been more than 60,000 votes short of winning a second seat in North Sumatra.

"I do not know why the PDI has suddenly received more than 60,000 additional votes. Where did these extra votes come from? Did they fall from the sky?," PPP Secretary-General Tosari Wijaya was quoted as saying by the Kompas daily.
Suryatna Subrata, secretary-general of the government's General Election Committee, was quoted in the Jakarta Post on Sunday as saying information on the poll result from other sources was invalid.
"Valid poll results (will be known on Monday) when we open the sealed election reports from the 27 provincial election committees," Subrata said on Saturday.

Provisional results of the poll after the counting of 115 million ballots had shown the Golkar party won 325 seats in the House, the PPP 89 and the PDI 10. The final results will be announced on June 23.

The drastic drop in the PDI's vote followed a split in the volatile Christian-Nationalist alliance last year, which led to ousted leader Megawati Sukarnoputri urging supporters to boycott its campaign and not vote for the government-recognised faction.
Megawati and her supporters were not officially recognised and not allowed to run in the tightly controlled poll.
